annotations.title: Prepare the value added tax return

description:
Prepare a French company's VAT return (CA3) for one period from its books, as a filled draft PDF stored in the workspace. Well prepares the return and fills it on impots.gouv.fr in the person's own Chrome; the person clicks Send and files it. This call files, sends and pays nothing. The PDF is the input of the `fill-ca3` browser skill, which types it into the online form and stops before Send.

Call it when the person asks to prepare or file their VAT return, after the VAT position of the period was read with `well_get_vat_summary`. Pass no window for the last period that has ended (the previous month for a monthly filer, the previous quarter for a quarterly one), or `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-01, `to` exclusive) for one named period.

The period follows the company's filing frequency from its tax profile:
- `status: "frequency_unknown"`: the profile holds no filing frequency. Propose a frequency only when a read returned one: the `filing_frequency` or `filing.cadence` of `well_get_vat_summary`, the months of the posted VAT entries it returned when they show a monthly or a quarterly rhythm, or a VAT return the person filed or uploaded (never a draft Well printed). With none, ask in one question whether the company files monthly or quarterly. Save it with `well_upsert_accounting_settings` only on their yes, and call again. Never save a frequency the person did not confirm.
- `status: "fiscal_start_unset"`: Well cannot place this return in a fiscal year. Ask the person to set the fiscal year start month in the workspace's accounting settings, then call again. The reply says: "Set the fiscal year start month in the workspace's accounting settings before reading fiscal periods."
- `no_vat_return`: the company is in the VAT franchise and files no VAT return. `annual_return`: it files one annual CA12, which Well does not prepare.
- `period_not_ended`: a month of the window is still running. Well prepares no return before its period ends.
- `not_return_periods` or `invalid_window`: the window is not whole return periods of the company's frequency.
- `several_returns`: the window holds several periods. `periods` lists them: one return per period, so prepare each with its own call.

Then the figures, read the same way as `well_get_vat_summary`. `basis` says what they were read on:
- `posted`: the posted ledger.
- `draft`: one invoice of the period, or more, has no posted VAT entry, so the figures add the draft entries and the VAT the invoices state. These amounts are not posted. Say so in one line with the figures, and before any fill ask the one question « Ces montants ne sont pas comptabilisés. Je remplis quand même ? »; the fill starts only on the person's yes to it.
- `gaps` on an `ok` result: the draft prints what the books place and leaves out each figure listed. `no_vat_found`: no entry and no invoice of the period states VAT, so every box is empty; this is not a nil return. From the ledger: `unattributed_collected_vat`, `unattributed_deductible_vat`, `unmapped_rate_percent`, `directionless_taxable_base`, `reverse_charge_present`, `negative_line`. From the invoices: `unsided_documents` (the side is not confirmed), `purchase_to_check_documents` (a supplier not shown to be French; its VAT is not deducted), `rate_unread_documents` (VAT not split by rate, or a line with no amount before tax), `tax_unknown_documents` (VAT never read), `other_currency_documents`, `null_currency_documents`, `undated_documents`. Give the figures, then say in plain words, one line each, what the draft leaves out and what to fix. A draft with gaps fails its check, so the fill waits until the gaps are fixed and the return is prepared again: offer no fill on it.
- `unsupported_jurisdiction` (not France), `unsupported_currency` (the books are not kept in EUR), `range_too_large`, `failed`: no PDF.

Line 22 carries the VAT credit the prior return carried forward. Well reads it from its own return of the prior period, or else from a return the person uploaded for that period; `prior_credit.source` says which (`prior_filed`, `prior_draft`, `prior_upload`, `person` or `none`):
- `prior_filed`: the credit of Well's own return of that period, marked filed. Ask nothing about it.
- `prior_draft`: the credit of the return Well prepared for that period, which Well never saw filed. Say so in one clause and ask once whether the return that was filed carried that credit forward.
- `prior_upload`: the amount is the refund that return shows, assumed to be the credit carried. Say so in one clause and ask once whether it is the credit that return carried forward.
- `none`: Well holds no prior return, so line 22 stays blank. Ask once whether the prior return carried a credit forward, and how much.
- For `prior_draft`, `prior_upload` and `none`, ask that question first, with the figures, as « le crédit reporté de ta déclaration précédente », naming no line or box, and offer no « 1. Valider » yet: no filing types a line 22 the person did not confirm. On the answer, call again for the same period with `prior_credit_euros` (0 when there was no credit), show the new figures, and offer « 1. Valider » only on those. Never pass an amount the person did not give.

On `ok`: `document_id` names the PDF, the value of the `document` input of the `fill-ca3` skill. `lines` lists every filled box by its printed line code and column, in whole euros. `vat_collected` and `vat_deductible` are the two totals, and `vat_due` (line TD) or `vat_credit` (line 25) is the result. `checks` lists what the person checks before filing: say what each one asks the person to check, in plain words. The line in a check's id is for Well's PDF: the reply never writes it (no « ligne 19 », no « ligne A2 »), because a printed box comes only from a rule `well_verify_tax_declaration` returns as failed. Never say the return is filed.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

from.description: First day of the period, YYYY-MM-01. Give it with `to`, or omit both for the last period that has ended.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

prior_credit_euros.description: The VAT credit the prior return carried forward, in whole euros, as the person stated it (0 for none). Only after asking the person; never an estimate.

to.description: EXCLUSIVE end: the first day of the month after the period, YYYY-MM-01.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_prepare_vat_return

basis.description: `posted`: the posted ledger. `draft`: these amounts are not posted; say so before any fill.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

gaps.description: What the draft leaves out. Empty when the books give the whole return; a draft with gaps cannot be filled.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

euros.description: The credit on line 22 in whole euros, zero when line 22 is blank.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

vat_collected.description: The gross VAT collected (line 16) in whole euros.

vat_credit.description: Line 25 in whole euros, zero when VAT is due.

vat_deductible.description: The deductible VAT (line 23) in whole euros.

vat_due.description: Line TD in whole euros, zero when the return shows a credit.

title: Prepare the value added tax return
